raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
**Why.** With `nccl_ub=True`, `_ParamAndGradBuffer.__init__` calls `torch.distributed.barrier()` with no group before and after its warmup `all_reduce` on the buffer's data-parallel group. It does this once per buffer. A rank builds one buffer per (param dtype, grad dtype, expert-parallel) key of its own model chunk, so its WORLD barrier count depends on its own parameters.
- In an MoE or hybrid model with a dense-only pipeline stage, that stage has no expert buffer. Each expert buffer adds 2 WORLD barriers on the MoE stages that the dense stage never enters.
- MIMO modules each wrap their own DDP on their own grid, so their ranks enter different counts too.
- The extra barriers wait on ranks that never reach them, or pair with a later default-group collective. Setup hangs, or later collectives cross-pair.
- The WORLD communicator is not one the memory pool registers on, so the WORLD barrier warms nothing that registration uses.

**What.**
- Pass `group=self.data_parallel_group` to both barriers in `megatron/core/distributed/param_and_grad_buffer.py`. That is the group of the warmup `all_reduce` and of the NCCL memory-pool registration.
- Every rank of that group is a data-parallel replica of the same model chunk. It builds the same buffers in the same order.
- Those ranks already enter the warmup `all_reduce` on this group at this point. The barriers sit on the same path, so exactly the group's ranks enter them, once per buffer.
- Dense buffers keep the intra DP x CP group and expert buffers the intra expert-DP group.

**Tests.**
- New `test_nccl_ub_warmup_syncs_only_the_data_parallel_group[gloo|nccl]` in `tests/unit_tests/distributed/test_param_and_grad_buffer.py`. It makes each half of the world its own data-parallel group. The first half builds 2 buffers with `nccl_ub=True` and the second half builds 1. The NCCL allocator is mocked. Collectives on the rank's own group run for real, and any collective on another group is recorded and skipped, so main fails instead of hanging.
- On 4 CPU ranks with Gloo, the `[gloo]` case passes on this branch and on 2 ranks. On main with only the new test added, it fails on every rank: ranks 0 and 1 report 4 group-less barriers, ranks 2 and 3 report 2.
- On 4 GPUs with NCCL, the whole file gives 99 passed and 4 skipped on this branch, and 97 passed and 4 skipped on main. The 2 extra passes are the new `[gloo]` and `[nccl]` cases.
- The whole file on 4 CPU ranks gives 81 passed, 17 failed, 5 skipped on this branch. Main with the new test gives 80 passed, 18 failed, 5 skipped. The extra failure on main is the new test. The other 17 fail on CPU with "Torch not compiled with CUDA" and are the same set on both.
- No DDP run with `--use-nccl-ub` and real NCCL memory pools was done on GPUs. No unit or functional test covers that path today.
- `tools/check_process_group_usage.py` reports the same 3 pre-existing entries before and after.
- `tools/check_kernel_determinism_coverage.py` flags the file under `ddp_grad_buffer_reductions`, hence `determinism-exempt`. The change only scopes two barriers and does not touch any reduction.

**Compatibility.**
- Without `nccl_ub`, nothing changes.
- With `nccl_ub`, the warmup no longer synchronizes ranks outside the buffer's data-parallel group. When every rank owns the same buffers, the only difference is that the barriers are on smaller groups.

Part of #6307.

- In an MoE or hybrid model with a dense-only pipeline stage, that stage has no expert buffer. Each expert buffer adds 2 WORLD barriers on the MoE stages that the dense stage never enters.
- MIMO modules each wrap their own DDP on their own grid, so their ranks enter different counts too.
- The extra barriers wait on ranks that never reach them, or pair with a later default-group collective. Setup hangs, or later collectives cross-pair.
- The WORLD communicator is not one the memory pool registers on, so the WORLD barrier warms nothing that registration uses.

**What.**
- Pass `group=self.data_parallel_group` to both barriers in `megatron/core/distributed/param_and_grad_buffer.py`. That is the group of the warmup `all_reduce` and of the NCCL memory-pool registration.
- Every rank of that group is a data-parallel replica of the same model chunk. It builds the same buffers in the same order.
- Those ranks already enter the warmup `all_reduce` on this group at this point. The barriers sit on the same path, so exactly the group's ranks enter them, once per buffer.
- Dense buffers keep the intra DP x CP group and expert buffers the intra expert-DP group.

**Tests.**
- New `test_nccl_ub_warmup_syncs_only_the_data_parallel_group[gloo|nccl]` in `tests/unit_tests/distributed/test_param_and_grad_buffer.py`. It makes each half of the world its own data-parallel group. The first half builds 2 buffers with `nccl_ub=True` and the second half builds 1. The NCCL allocator is mocked. Collectives on the rank's own group run for real, and any collective on another group is recorded and skipped, so main fails instead of hanging.
- On 4 CPU ranks with Gloo, the `[gloo]` case passes on this branch and on 2 ranks. On main with only the new test added, it fails on every rank: ranks 0 and 1 report 4 group-less barriers, ranks 2 and 3 report 2.
- On 4 GPUs with NCCL, the whole file gives 99 passed and 4 skipped on this branch, and 97 passed and 4 skipped on main. The 2 extra passes are the new `[gloo]` and `[nccl]` cases.
- The whole file on 4 CPU ranks gives 81 passed, 17 failed, 5 skipped on this branch. Main with the new test gives 80 passed, 18 failed, 5 skipped. The extra failure on main is the new test. The other 17 fail on CPU with "Torch not compiled with CUDA" and are the same set on both.
- No DDP run with `--use-nccl-ub` and real NCCL memory pools was done on GPUs. No unit or functional test covers that path today.
- `tools/check_process_group_usage.py` reports the same 3 pre-existing entries before and after.
- `tools/check_kernel_determinism_coverage.py` flags the file under `ddp_grad_buffer_reductions`, hence `determinism-exempt`. The change only scopes two barriers and does not touch any reduction.

- Without `nccl_ub`, nothing changes.
- With `nccl_ub`, the warmup no longer synchronizes ranks outside the buffer's data-parallel group. When every rank owns the same buffers, the only difference is that the barriers are on smaller groups.

files.patch:
@@ -1232,10 +1232,12 @@ def __init__(
             )
             # Since nccl communicator group is created lazily, we need to perform a warmup call to
             # initialize NCCL comm buffers for this dp_group before doing buffer registration.
-            torch.distributed.barrier()
+            # Barriers stay on dp_group: ranks outside it (other PP stages, other modules) may
+            # own a different number of buffers, so a WORLD barrier here would not pair up.
+            torch.distributed.barrier(group=self.data_parallel_group)
             tmp_warmup_tensor = torch.zeros([1], device="cuda")
             torch.distributed.all_reduce(tmp_warmup_tensor, group=self.data_parallel_group)
-            torch.distributed.barrier()
+            torch.distributed.barrier(group=self.data_parallel_group)
         else:
             # If nccl_ub is False, the allocation context is nullcontext.
             mem_alloc_context = nullcontext

@@ -1090,3 +1090,104 @@ def test_expert_parallel_params_get_separate_buffers(use_distributed_optimizer:
             )
 
     Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("backend", ["gloo", "nccl"])
+def test_nccl_ub_warmup_syncs_only_the_data_parallel_group(backend: str):
+    """The NCCL user-buffer warmup must only synchronize the buffer's data-parallel group.
+
+    Ranks outside that group, such as other pipeline stages or other MIMO modules, can own a
+    different number of buffers. Each half of the world is its own data-parallel group here:
+    the first half builds two buffers and the second half builds one. A WORLD barrier in the
+    warmup would be entered twice as often by the first half, so it would hang or pair with an
+    unrelated collective. The NCCL allocator is mocked; the warmup collectives on each rank's
+    own group run for real.
+    """
+    if backend == "nccl" and not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("The NCCL backend needs CUDA.")
+    Utils.initialize_distributed()
+    world_size = torch.distributed.get_world_size()
+    if world_size % 2 != 0:
+        pytest.skip("Needs an even number of ranks.")
+
+    rank = torch.distributed.get_rank()
+    half = world_size // 2
+    # new_group is collective over WORLD, so every rank creates both groups in the same order.
+    half_groups = [
+        torch.distributed.new_group(ranks=list(range(half)), backend=backend),
+        torch.distributed.new_group(ranks=list(range(half, world_size)), backend=backend),
+    ]
+    dp_group = half_groups[0] if rank < half else half_groups[1]
+    num_buffers = 2 if rank < half else 1
+
+    calls = []
+
+    def run_on_dp_group_only(name, real_fn):
+        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
+            group = kwargs.get("group")
+            calls.append((name, group))
+            # A collective on any other group would wait for ranks that never reach it, so
+            # record it and skip it instead of hanging the test.
+            if group is dp_group:
+                return real_fn(*args, **kwargs)
+            return None
+
+        return wrapper
+
+    patches = [
+        mock.patch("megatron.core.distributed.param_and_grad_buffer.nccl_allocator"),
+        mock.patch(
+            "torch.distributed.barrier",
+            side_effect=run_on_dp_group_only("barrier", torch.distributed.barrier),
+        ),
+        mock.patch(
+            "torch.distributed.all_reduce",
+            side_effect=run_on_dp_group_only("all_reduce", torch.distributed.all_reduce),
+        ),
+    ]
+    device = "cuda"
+    if backend == "gloo":
+        device = "cpu"
+        real_zeros = torch.zeros
+
+        def zeros_on_cpu(*args, **kwargs):
+            kwargs["device"] = "cpu"
+            return real_zeros(*args, **kwargs)
+
+        patches += [
+            mock.patch("torch.cuda.current_device", return_value="cpu"),
+            mock.patch("torch.zeros", side_effect=zeros_on_cpu),
+        ]
+
+    ddp_config = DistributedDataParallelConfig(
+        nccl_ub=True,
+        use_distributed_optimizer=False,
+        overlap_grad_reduce=False,
+        bucket_size=None,
+        average_in_collective=False,
+    )
+    with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
+        for patch in patches:
+            stack.enter_context(patch)
+        for buffer_index in range(num_buffers):
+            param = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.randn(8, 8, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device))
+            name = f"layer{buffer_index}.weight"
+            _ParamAndGradBuffer(
+                ddp_config=ddp_config,
+                param_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+                grad_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+                params_with_names=[(param, name)],
+                data_parallel_group=dp_group,
+                bucket_size=None,
+                param_to_name={param: name},
+                gradient_scaling_factor=1.0,
+                param_indices=[0],
+                nccl_ub=True,
+                pg_collection=mock.MagicMock(),
+            )
+
+    assert any(name == "all_reduce" for name, _ in calls), "The warmup did not run"
+    off_group = [name for name, group in calls if group is not dp_group]
+    assert (
+        not off_group
+    ), f"NCCL user-buffer warmup issued {off_group} outside the buffer's data-parallel group"
